base.description: For a pull, the branch it targets from here on, without refs/heads/: set when the branch it targeted was renamed, or went as the pull with that head branch landed.

from.description: For `merged`, the hex object ID the base was at before the merge: from..commit is what the pull brought in, whose commits readers may then show as its author's.

pull.description: For `closed` on an issue, the dev.knotless.pull whose merge closed it, as its title or body named the issue after a closing keyword such as `Fixes`. Beside `since`, the pull a pull was moved off as it landed.

repo.description: The repository the pull or issue is on.

batch.description: For `merged` by a merge queue, the hex object ID of the tip of the batch it landed in: the commit whose checks let it land. The pulls merged with the same `batch` were checked and landed together.

since.description: Beside `base`, for a pull moved there as the pull it was built on landed: that pull's head, the hex object ID its own changes start from.

state.description: `merged` applies to pulls only; `resolved` and `open`, to a thread. Absent when the record only sets `base`: the state stands.

commit.description: The hex object ID of the merge commit, for `merged`.

subject.description: The dev.knotless.pull or dev.knotless.issue whose state changed; or the dev.knotless.comment, with a `line`, that starts a thread.

main.description: Kept in the account of whoever changed it. Readers take the latest from someone allowed to make it: the subject's author, the repository's owner or a collaborator; `merged` only from the latter two; for a thread, also the pull's author.

description: A pull or issue opened, closed or merged, or a pull pointed at another target branch; or a thread on a pull's lines resolved or opened again.
